stem.en: Arrange the following levels of organisation in a multicellular organism in order, from the smallest structural unit to the level capable of carrying out the largest body-wide functions.

text.en: Cells, then tissues, then organs, then the organism.
Cells, then organs, then tissues, then the organism.

feedback.en: Organs are built from tissues, so tissues must be the level below organs, not above them.

text.en: Tissues, then cells, then organs, then the organism.

feedback.en: A tissue is a group of cells, so the cell cannot be the larger unit.

text.en: Cells, then tissues, then the organism, then organs.

feedback.en: The organism is the complete individual and therefore the highest level of the four.

explanation.en:
**Why "cells, tissues, organs, organism" is correct**

Each level is built from the level below it. A group of similar cells performing a common function constitutes a tissue; several different tissues held together and performing one larger activity constitute an organ; organs working together constitute the organism.

**Why the remaining options are incorrect**

- **Cells, organs, tissues, organism** - reverses the tissue and organ levels. An organ cannot exist before the tissues that compose it.
- **Tissues, cells, organs, organism** - places the tissue below the cell, although a tissue is a group of cells.
- **Cells, tissues, organism, organs** - places the organ above the whole organism.

hints.en: Ask, at each level, what the level is made of.
